checks.result: The exact Rust surface is formatted and the Windows desktop library passes Clippy with warnings denied, compiling and linking the production CredUI, LogonUserW, process-token, SID, handle, and secret-zeroization adapter path.

All 12 focused renderer/application tests passed. The strict decoder accepts only six fixed outcomes with allowed redacted reason codes, requires a native succeeded/unlocked or adverse/locked pairing, rejects unknown/prototype and forged state combinations, and preserves the existing cancellation, rate-limit, Core-unavailable, and generic password failure copy.
Desktop TypeScript type checking and the repository desktop lint passed for the typed application-unlock response and renderer integration.

All four focused security/source and portable profile-contract tests passed. They pin the non-persisting Windows prompt flags, NameSamCompatible prefill, local/down-level and UPN domain mapping, LogonUserW, current-process token and EqualSid checks, handle closure, volatile buffer clearing, argument-free native unlock bridge, generation binding, protected-command guards, and unchanged strict application-lock profile.

The machine-checked architecture contract passed with 13 repository areas, 12 modules, five stable interfaces, and three deployment profiles; the provider seam did not cross or weaken a declared application/renderer/Core boundary.
The directly changed Python security tests pass Ruff lint and formatting, and the exact implementation range passes Git whitespace hygiene.

The governed changed-path selector passed with no unknown paths and retained desktop performance at W1 exit. Risk-selected task checks were narrowed to the native/provider, typed renderer, Windows credential-source, portable profile, architecture, formatting, lint, and type surfaces that can plausibly fail from T01.

evidence: application_lock_unlock remains an argument-free Tauri command, constructs no renderer-selected provider or outcome, and emits an unlocked snapshot only when the native manager returns VerificationOutcome::Succeeded.

The native manager reserves exactly one locked-generation attempt, invokes the provider once, rechecks the reservation before and after Core start, publishes Unlocked only after RuntimeState::Ready, and immediately stop_for_application_lock on stale or failed Core startup. Protected native operations still require the manager-owned lock generation, so renderer data cannot confer native authority.

WindowsPasswordVerificationProvider implements the provider-neutral native interface and owns the existing OS credential prompt, identity parsing, LogonUserW validation, current desktop process token lookup, and EqualSid comparison.

Windows tests and source assertions retain ALWAYS_SHOW_UI, DO_NOT_PERSIST, EXCLUDE_CERTIFICATES, GENERIC_CREDENTIALS, and VALIDATE_USERNAME flags; NameSamCompatible prefill; null UPN domain versus retained down-level domain; volatile username/domain/password clearing; and RAII handle closure. A mismatched returned token remains Denied and can never produce Succeeded.

The native VerificationOutcome serializes exactly succeeded, cancelled, denied, unavailable, busy, and failed. The manager has an explicit fail-closed branch for each value, starts Core only for succeeded, never invokes another provider, and retains a locked snapshot for every adverse outcome.

The application contract strictly decodes the same six outcomes and fixed redacted reason codes, rejects outcome/state mismatches and unknown/prototype outcomes, and permits fail-closed reconciliation to clear only from a succeeded native unlock response carrying an unlocked native snapshot.

The password adapter preserves absent-profile startup, zero-minute unlocked startup, nonzero-timeout restart lock, corrupt-profile fail lock, manual and native-idle lock, generation invalidation, one-attempt admission, denial backoff, cancellation, Core restart failure, fresh-Core/no-project restoration behavior, and content-free fixed-code audit behavior.

The renderer retains the exact user-visible cancellation, temporary rate-limit, accepted-credentials/Core-unavailable, and generic verification-failure messages. Expected adverse provider results now arrive as typed native attempts; unexpected bridge failures still reconcile through native status and fail closed.

Production changes are confined to the application-lock coordinator, a new native verification-provider module, the argument-free native bridge, directly affected renderer contract/runtime code, and focused tests. The portable application-lock profile bytes and schema are unchanged.

No Windows Hello implementation, sign-in configuration, settings route/UI, project security, encryption, privacy, identity, Core supervision redesign, dependency, migration, or governed experience-reference change is included.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: W1.A05.T01 changes a native Windows authentication boundary, the success-to-Core-restart authority transition, and the typed renderer/native contract. Credible failures are renderer/provider substitution, collapsed adverse outcomes, stale or concurrent success, Core creation after invalidation, same-SID regression, credential persistence or leakage, reservation/backoff corruption, unlocked invocation, and user-visible error disclosure. Full native library tests, warnings-denied compilation, strict renderer contract tests, desktop lint/type checking, focused Windows credential and portable profile assertions, architecture checks, changed-test quality, and Git hygiene cover those risks. The task does not change dependencies, persistence schemas, project data, UI structure, or approved experience references.
